pr_body:
If debug logging is enabled then the lag detector will capture and report the hot threads of a lagging node. In some cases the resulting log message can be very large, exceeding 10kiB, which means it is truncated in most logging setups. The relevant thread(s) may be waiting on I/O, which is not considered "hot" and therefore may not appear in the first 10kiB.

This commit adjusts this logging mechanism to split the message into chunks of size at most 2kiB (after compression and base64-encoding) to ensure that the entire hot threads output can be faithfully reconstructed from these logs.

Closes #88126
pr_title: Limit length of lag detector hot threads log lines
pr_comment: Hi @DaveCTurner, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

review_comment: Would it make sense to make this an undocumented configurable setting?
This functionality only really makes sense for debugging, and I don't see a great reason to want to change this.

I've thought about this a little more and I now see value in adding some configurability here. Particularly the `NodesHotThreadsRequest` we use has some hard-coded parameters & defaults that deserve to be exposed as settings, and if we're adding those settings then why not this one too?

I won't do it in this PR tho, nor do I expect to get to it any time soon, but if you're interested then feel free to open a follow-up.

I think 2KiB is reasonable. And since now we have some quick commands to reconstruct it, I think it is fine. Originally I had thought (before I realized of the econding) that I could have set this to something large, so that there would be one big block of human-readable text. But since now either way we need to process the encoded text, I do not mind the chunks. We can make this configurable if the need ever arises.
I guess the standard charset here encompasses all the safe bytes mentioned below?

Yes, [ISO-8859-1](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/ISO/IEC_8859-1) agrees with US-ASCII (and hence UTF-8) on these bytes, and is the encoding that Java uses internally which makes this the most efficient way to construct a `String` from some bytes.
I guess here you're trying to test different lengths around the chunk size?
This description has similar text to the class description. Maybe consolidate in one place?
I think we need Javadoc in both places. Is there a way to share common chunks of Javadoc?
Could link to the class or link the function from the class, but it is not that important.

I am not sure if there could be many of these tasks piling up in the prioritized thread runner, but just in case, would it make sense to capture the timestamp on task creation and use it to prioritize earlier tasks higher?
They shouldn't pile up much, but even if they do it's a `PriorityBlockingQueue` which yields tasks of equal priority in FIFO order.
